assets.notes: gilyon/snes-tests 65816 CPU test ROMs (cputest-basic.sfc: 1107 tests, skips undocumented emulation-mode wrapping edge cases; cputest-full.sfc: 1610 tests, includes them). Both report results via a text shell (Success / Failed #N with register dump), verified by the rom_runner screen-CRC oracle against a human-approved PASS capture. Both currently PASS in this emulator (visually confirmed against Mesen2 running the same ROM files) — one test per ROM in snes::integration_tests::gilyon_cpu_tests.

variants.notes: Vendored release build of cputest-basic.sfc and cputest-full.sfc plus their generated docs/assembly (tests-*.txt, tests-*.inc, tests_table.inc).

assets.notes: blargg (Shay Green) SNES SPC700/APU test ROMs. They report results via blargg's standard text shell (Passed / Failed #N / Internal error), so the committed subset is verified by comparing the rendered screen CRC32 at a fixed frame against a human-approved PASS capture (NESER_CAPTURE_SCREEN). License is informal: these are freely-redistributable test binaries with no formal license file, recorded as unknown; author site http://www.slack.net/~ant/. All 18 ROMs are committed and all 18 currently PASS in this emulator with visually-approved screen-CRC goldens, one test per ROM (blargg_rom_test! in blargg_apu_tests.rs). timer_at_power_reset requires a mid-test soft reset when the ROM jumps to $0000 (modeled via RunConfig::with_reset_on_pc_trap); spc_dsp6 needs an extended 600M-tick budget and runs to frame 9100. See README-SNES for details.

variants.notes: All 18 blargg SPC700/APU ROMs have visually-approved PASS goldens run by snes::integration_tests::blargg_apu_tests with the screen-CRC oracle, one test per ROM.

assets.notes: undisbeliever (Marcus Rowe) SNES hardware-glitch/timing-hammer test ROMs. Unlike blargg/gilyon, these do not print a PASS/FAIL text screen -- the upstream source documents them as hardware race demonstrations ('you may need to reset your console a few times for the glitch to appear') or interactive demos, so there is no canonical correct screen even on real hardware. 12 of the 29 vendored ROMs are automated: each golden is a stability snapshot of the ROM's default (no-input) rendering, cross-checked against a Mesen2 capture of the identical ROM file (using --Video.VideoFilter=None --Video.AspectRatio=NoStretching, and allowing for a harmless constant 1-scanline row offset between the two emulators' screenshot conventions) -- not proof of hardware accuracy. See snes::integration_tests::undisbeliever_tests. The other 17 ROMs showed real NESER-vs-Mesen2 divergences during this cross-check and are deliberately left un-automated pending fixes: hdmaen_latch_test(_2).sfc, inidisp_brightness_delay.sfc, hdma-2100-glitch-2ch-{0a,81}.sfc, hdma-21ff-2100-glitch.sfc (issue #2943, likely finer within-scanline HDMA timing than the once-per-scanline model added for #2945/#2947 covers); inidisp_forgot_to_force_blank.sfc (issue #2944, missing VRAM/OAM corruption from writes outside force-blank -- inidisp_enable_display_mid_frame.sfc from the same issue was fixed and automated once per-scanline INIDISP latching landed, see #2947); all 10 scpu-a-dma-bug-*.sfc (issue #2945, the break/COP crash is fixed but the HDMA-driven scanline-brightness banding isn't yet phase-accurate against Mesen2). See README-SNES.md for the full breakdown.

variants.notes: All 29 ROMs are vendored; 12 have visually-approved stability-snapshot goldens run by snes::integration_tests::undisbeliever_tests with the screen-CRC oracle, one test per ROM. The remaining 17 are committed but not yet automated (see notes above and #2943/#2944/#2945).
